set.body:
Measured residual after monomorphic closeout (modules/benchmarks/results/2026-07-28-local-jdk25-closeout/): compute geomean 0.824x NumPy meets the 0.50x primary target, but stretch (0.70x / no case below 0.50x) fails because the reduction family geomeans at 0.392x (worst full_sum_inner_stride 0.293x; axis1 ~0.30-0.39x). Exact-schedule axis1 reuse controls already sit near ~0.38-0.43x NumPy, so further pairwise scalar tuning will not close the gap.

Decision needed before implementation:
1) JDK Vector API / Panama for contiguous float64 add and (optionally) associative reduction loops, JVM-only with scalar fallback.
2) Opt-in fast reduction policy (e.g. sumFast / Associative / kernel-only) that may change association vs the default bit-stable 128-block pairwise schedule; default public sum unchanged.
3) Explicitly accept reduction family ~0.3-0.45x as a documented numerical-contract tax and stop until a later major version.

Acceptance for this decision bead: choose one primary path with a written rationale, file follow-on implementation beads, and keep NumPy semantic parity as the hard gate. Do not change default pairwise semantics without an explicit public API opt-in.
set.title: Decide residual NumPy gap: Vector API and/or opt-in fast reductions
